sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar for the second day of Shavuos 5728.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
The second day of the festival of Shavuos, 5728.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Alter Rebbe's question on the verse "And G-d spoke all these words, saying: I am..." and his answer that the Ten Commandments contain the entire Torah in a general principle, which is then detailed.

translations.translation: "And G-d spoke all these words, saying: I am..."
And the Alter Rebbe
questions the meaning of "all these words,"
for seemingly it should have said, "And G-d spoke, I am..."
And he explains,
that "all these words" refers
to the entire Torah,
including everything that a veteran student will innovate in the future.
And this is "And G-d spoke all these words,"
for in the Ten Commandments
the entire Torah is included
("all these words").
And this can be connected with Rashi's commentary on the verse,
that what is written "all these words"
(before "I am...")
teaches that all the Ten Commandments were said
(initially)
in one utterance,
and afterwards each and every commandment was explained individually.
For the content of both explanations is,
that the giving of the Torah was in a manner of general principle and detail.
However, according to Rashi's explanation, the verse speaks of the Ten Commandments themselves,
that initially they were said in a general aspect
(one utterance)
and afterwards each and every commandment was detailed individually.
And according to the Alter Rebbe's explanation, the verse speaks of the details of the Torah,
that they too were given initially in a general aspect,
in the Ten Commandments,
and afterwards they were detailed and drawn down into revelation.
And one may add,
that even this itself
(the detailing and revelation of the Ten Commandments)
was in a manner of general principle and detail.
For the beginning of the drawing down and detailing of the Ten Commandments is in the Written Torah,
and afterwards it is detailed more specifically in the Oral Torah,
for the entire Oral Torah is the explanation
and elucidation of the Written Torah
("From where are these matters? The verse says..."),
and the Oral Torah itself is also in a manner of general principle and detail,
Mishnah, Beraisa,
Gemara, etc., until everything that a veteran student will innovate.
And it needs to be understood,
since all the details of the Torah,
up to everything that a veteran student will innovate,
were all given to Moshe at Sinai,
why were they not given from the outset in a revealed manner,
and why were they given initially in a general aspect.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the creation of the world also followed a pattern of general principle and detail, as the general utterance of "Bereishis" contained all subsequent utterances.

translations.translation: B)
And this will be understood
from what we find similarly regarding the creation of the world
("He looked into the Torah and created the world"),
that it was in a manner of general principle and detail.
For our Sages said,
"With ten utterances the world was created... could it not have been created with one utterance?"
And it is known
that the "one utterance" is the utterance of "Bereishis"
("Bereishis is also an utterance"),
which is a general utterance that includes the nine utterances that follow it.
For this is what is written,
"In the beginning G-d created the heavens and the earth," and our Sages said,
"'the heavens' to include their hosts, and 'the earth' to include its hosts,"
that all creations came into being from the utterance of "Bereishis"
(as it is a general utterance that includes all the utterances).
However, they were in a general aspect,
and afterwards the utterance of "Bereishis" was detailed in the nine utterances that follow it,
and through this the creations came into being in a manner of division into details.
